title: Completion-unit tensor insertions and coherent pullback tensor comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ and the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$ and $u_c^*=C_{\mathcal X}u^*\dashv P$ on complete objects. For arbitrary $V,W\in D_T$ the maps
$$C_T(\eta_{T,V}\otimes1_W):C_T(V\otimes_A^LW)\longrightarrow C_T(C_TV\otimes_A^LW),\qquad C_T(1_V\otimes\eta_{T,W})$$
are natural isomorphisms, as is
$$C_{\mathcal X}u^*(\eta_{\mathcal Y,V}):C_{\mathcal X}u^*V\longrightarrow C_{\mathcal X}u^*C_{\mathcal Y}V.$$
On complete objects put $V\widehat\otimes W=C_T(V\otimes_A^LW)$. There is a unique natural completed pullback tensor comparison
$$\mu^c_{V,W}:C_{\mathcal X}u^*C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes_A^LW)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{\mathcal X}(C_{\mathcal X}u^*V\otimes_A^LC_{\mathcal X}u^*W)$$
whose composite with $C_{\mathcal X}u^*(\eta_{\mathcal Y,V\otimes W})$ equals $C_{\mathcal X}((\eta_{\mathcal X,u^*V}\otimes\eta_{\mathcal X,u^*W})\mu_{V,W})$, where $\mu$ is the ordinary pullback tensor comparison. These comparisons and the unit comparison induced from the ordinary tensor unit satisfy the associativity, symmetry and tensor-unit coherence equations. No perfectness of $A_n$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Suppress inclusions of the full complete subcategories, and write $H(W,Z)=R\mathcal Hom(W,Z)$ and $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$. The category $D_T$ is closed symmetric monoidal by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. For complete $Z$, [lem-sf-ringed-rhom-derived-complete] makes $H(W,Z)$ complete for arbitrary $W$. Reflectivity from [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] and the natural tensor–Hom bijection give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C_T(C_TV\otimes W),Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_TV,H(W,Z))\xrightarrow{\ -\circ\eta_V\ }\operatorname{Hom}(V,H(W,Z))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_T(V\otimes W),Z).$$
Every arrow is a bijection, and naturality identifies this composite with precomposition by $C_T(\eta_V\otimes1_W)$. Thus that arrow is invertible: for an arrow $f:B\to B'$ between complete objects, bijectivity of precomposition for $Z=B$ gives $t:B'\to B$ with $tf=1$; injectivity for $Z=B'$ then gives $ft=1$.

source.place: Tags 099A (lemma-derived-complete-internal-hom) and 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product); explicit Hom argument for the unit insertion.

proof.text: The same Hom calculation shows that if $C_Tg$ is invertible, then $C_T(g\otimes1_W)$ is invertible: replace $\eta_V$ by $g$, and use $\operatorname{Hom}(g,H(W,Z))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_Tg,H(W,Z))$. Symmetry from [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives the corresponding assertion for $C_T(1_W\otimes g)$. Apply this to $g=\eta_V$ or $\eta_W$ to obtain the other stated tensor insertion. Here $C_T\eta$ is invertible because reflection into a full subcategory is idempotent, directly by the unit-precomposition bijection of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. The insertions are natural by naturality of $\eta$ and bifunctoriality of tensor. Their composites include the natural isomorphism $m_{V,W}=C_T(\eta_V\otimes\eta_W)$.

source.place: Tag 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product), formal consequences of the preceding Hom calculation.

proof.text:
Put $L=u^*$ and $F=C_{\mathcal X}L$. For complete $Z\in D_{\mathcal X}$, [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] says that $PZ$ is complete and supplies the ordinary derived and completion adjunctions. Hence
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F C_{\mathcal Y}V,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\mathcal Y}V,PZ)\xrightarrow{\ -\circ\eta_V\ }\operatorname{Hom}(V,PZ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FV,Z).$$
Naturality identifies the composite with precomposition by $a_V=F(\eta_{\mathcal Y,V})$, so the inverse argument of step 1 proves that $a_V$ is an isomorphism. More generally $F$ inverts every arrow $g$ inverted by $C_{\mathcal Y}$: in this display replace $\eta_V$ by $g$ and use the reflection bijection for the complete object $PZ$. All these conclusions are natural in $V$.

source.place: Tags 099M (lemma-naive-completion) and 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), clauses (1),(2); formal Hom argument, without interchanging pullback and limits.

proof.text: The ordinary comparison $\mu$ in the statement respects associators, signed symmetry and the tensor unit. To verify precisely this normalization, use [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit]: on flat-term K-flat representatives its displayed formula identifies $\mu$ with the localized cochain comparison $c_{u;P,Q}$. By [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], that cochain comparison respects triple reassociation, signed symmetry and both action unitors. [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies every derived object with such a representative; therefore the equalities for each pair or triple of representatives give the equalities for arbitrary derived inputs, by naturality and conjugation with their representative isomorphisms. The ordinary constraints being compared are those of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Thus this is coherence for the specified ordinary $\mu$, rather than for an unspecified choice of tensor comparison.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product) and 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); normalized cochain equations supplied by the cited nodes.

proof.text:
Here are the completed constraints used in the conclusion. For complete $V,W,Z$, let $J_T=C_T\mathbf1_T$ and put
$$A=C_T(\eta_{V\otimes W}\otimes1_Z),\quad B=C_T(1_V\otimes\eta_{W\otimes Z}),\quad \alpha^c_{V,W,Z}=B\,C_T(\alpha_{V,W,Z})\,A^{-1},\quad\sigma^c_{V,W}=C_T(\sigma_{V,W}).$$
Define the left unitor by
$$\lambda^c_V=\eta_V^{-1}C_T(\lambda_V)\,C_T(\eta_{\mathbf1_T}\otimes1_V)^{-1}:C_T(J_T\otimes V)\longrightarrow V,$$
and the right unitor by $\rho^c_V=\eta_V^{-1}C_T(\rho_V)C_T(1_V\otimes\eta_{\mathbf1_T})^{-1}$. All inverses exist by steps 1–2 and completeness of $V$. These are natural isomorphisms by functoriality and the naturality of the ordinary constraints of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal].

source.place: Tag 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product); explicit constraints on its completed tensor, with unit the completion of the ordinary unit.

proof.text: Check the coherence of these constraints by the following explicit cancellation. For any fixed parenthesized tensor expression, insert $\eta$ at each internal tensor vertex and apply the outside $C_T$; the resulting map from the completion of the ordinary expression to the iterated completed expression is invertible, since each insertion is inverted by $C_T$ even after tensoring, by step 2. Naturality of $\eta$ and the formula for $\alpha^c$ in step 5 say that, across each reassociation edge, the composite is exactly $C_T$ of the ordinary reassociation followed by the insertion map for the new expression. Therefore both pentagon paths, precomposed with the same insertion isomorphism from the fourfold ordinary tensor, are $C_T$ of the ordinary pentagon paths followed by the same final insertion. They agree by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]; cancel the isomorphism. For the triangle use the ordinary threefold expression with middle factor $\mathbf1_T$, inserting $\eta_{\mathbf1_T}$ as well; the two paths reduce to its ordinary triangle. For the symmetry involution and hexagon the identical cancellation uses the twofold and threefold expressions respectively and the ordinary involution and hexagon. Thus all completed constraints satisfy their equations.

source.place: Tag 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product), explicit formal cancellation using the ordinary coherence equations of sites-cohomology Tag 0FPT.

proof.text:
Write $\kappa_V=\eta_{\mathcal X,LV}:LV\to FV$. For arbitrary $V,W$ define
$$b_{V,W}=C_{\mathcal X}(\kappa_V\otimes\kappa_W)\,C_{\mathcal X}(\mu_{V,W}),\qquad \mu^c_{V,W}=b_{V,W}\,a_{V\otimes W}^{-1}.$$
The maps $a$ are invertible by step 3; $b$ is invertible by the ordinary comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] and the two tensor insertions in steps 1–2. This gives exactly the displayed source and target in the statement. Naturality follows from that of $a,b$ and their inverses. The required equation is $\mu^c a=b$, by cancellation; conversely this equation forces $\mu^c=ba^{-1}$. It therefore gives uniqueness of the specified natural comparison, including when restricted to complete inputs.

source.place: Tag 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product); formal definition and uniqueness from the insertion isomorphisms.

proof.text:
We verify the associativity equation for $F$ on complete inputs $V,W,Z$. Precompose its left-associated source $F(C_{\mathcal Y}(C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes W)\otimes Z))$ with
$$F((V\otimes W)\otimes Z)\xrightarrow{F(\eta_{V\otimes W}\otimes1)}F(C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes W)\otimes Z)\xrightarrow{a_{C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes W)\otimes Z}}F(C_{\mathcal Y}(C_{\mathcal Y}(V\otimes W)\otimes Z)).$$
Both arrows are invertible: use steps 2–3 for the first and step 3 for the second. Expand each $\mu^c a=b$ and $\alpha^c=B C(\alpha)A^{-1}$. Cancel consecutive insertion maps and their inverses; move the remaining ones past each other using naturality of $\eta$. The left path becomes $C_{\mathcal X}$ of
$$(\kappa_V\otimes(\kappa_W\otimes\kappa_Z))\,\alpha_{LV,LW,LZ}\,(\mu_{V,W}\otimes1)\,\mu_{V\otimes W,Z},$$
and the right path becomes $C_{\mathcal X}$ of
$$(\kappa_V\otimes(\kappa_W\otimes\kappa_Z))\,(1\otimes\mu_{W,Z})\,\mu_{V,W\otimes Z}\,L(\alpha_{V,W,Z}),$$
each followed by the same insertion into the final iterated completed tensor. They agree by step 4. Cancel the source isomorphism to obtain the completed associativity equation.

source.place: Tag 099G (remark-completed-tensor-product); explicit associativity cancellation for the normalized comparison.

proof.text:
For symmetry, precompose the comparison equation with $a_{V\otimes W}$. By naturality $F C_{\mathcal Y}(\sigma)\,a_{V\otimes W}=a_{W\otimes V}\,F(\sigma)$. Substitute $\mu^c a=b$ on both sides. The two resulting arrows are
$$C_{\mathcal X}((\kappa_W\otimes\kappa_V)\,\sigma_{LV,LW}\,\mu_{V,W}),\qquad C_{\mathcal X}((\kappa_W\otimes\kappa_V)\,\mu_{W,V}\,L(\sigma_{V,W})).$$
They agree by step 4, so cancel $a_{V\otimes W}$. For the unit let $e:L\mathbf1_{\mathcal Y}\cong\mathbf1_{\mathcal X}$ be the ordinary unit comparison and define
$$e^c=C_{\mathcal X}(e)\,a_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal Y}}^{-1}:FJ_{\mathcal Y}\longrightarrow J_{\mathcal X}.$$
It is invertible. To check the left unit equation precompose its source $F(C_{\mathcal Y}(J_{\mathcal Y}\otimes V))$ with the isomorphism $a_{J_{\mathcal Y}\otimes V}F(\eta_{\mathbf1_{\mathcal Y}}\otimes1_V)$ from $F(\mathbf1_{\mathcal Y}\otimes V)$. Substitute step 5 and $\mu^c a=b$; naturality of $\eta$ cancels its insertions, leaving $C_{\mathcal X}(\kappa_V\,\lambda_{LV}(e\otimes1)\mu_{\mathbf1,V})=C_{\mathcal X}(\kappa_V L\lambda_V)$. Both sides have the same final identification $\eta_{FV}^{-1}:C_{\mathcal X}(FV)\to FV$. This is the ordinary unit equation of step 4. The right unit equation uses $F(1_V\otimes\eta_{\mathbf1})$ and the ordinary right unitor in exactly the same substitution, leaving $C_{\mathcal X}(\kappa_V\,\rho_{LV}(1\otimes e)\mu_{V,\mathbf1})=C_{\mathcal X}(\kappa_V L\rho_V)$. Apply the same final identification $\eta_{FV}^{-1}$ and cancel the respective source isomorphisms. No step used perfectness of $A/I^n$.
